mismatch_adjudications.canonical_behavior: Reject non-finite helper inputs with the normalized invalid_decimal category.
mismatch_adjudications.characterization: Python previously returned non-finite values or leaked decimal.InvalidOperation while Rust returned FeeError::InvalidDecimal.
mismatch_adjudications.compatibility_impact: Finite fee calculations are unchanged; callers passing NaN or infinity now receive a stable Python ValueError instead of a non-JSON result or decimal implementation error.

mismatch_adjudications.canonical_behavior: Round signed trade-fee values to the next centicent toward positive infinity, matching Decimal ROUND_CEILING.
mismatch_adjudications.characterization: Python used ROUND_CEILING for every sign while Rust used AwayFromZero, which lowered negative values by an extra centicent.
mismatch_adjudications.compatibility_impact: Positive fee calculations are unchanged; negative quantity, multiplier, or fee inputs now produce the same less-negative ceiling in Rust as Python.

mismatch_adjudications.canonical_behavior: Reject action values outside buy/sell and liquidity roles outside maker/taker with stable normalized helper errors.
mismatch_adjudications.characterization: Rust closed enums already rejected unknown values, while Python Literal annotations were static-only and silently treated unknown values as alternate valid branches.
mismatch_adjudications.compatibility_impact: Valid helper calls are unchanged; invalid Python runtime strings now raise ValueError instead of producing a fee result.

mismatch_adjudications.canonical_behavior: Direct exported Literal domains enumerate their complete vocabulary and reject unknown serialized values in both languages.
mismatch_adjudications.characterization: Several Python Literal exports were represented by unconstrained Rust String aliases, so their direct Rust boundary accepted values that Python rejected.
mismatch_adjudications.compatibility_impact: The affected direct Rust exports are now enums. Upstream response fields deliberately typed as Literal | str remain String-backed and forward compatible; ReportType fields, which are closed in Python, are closed in Rust as well.

export_groups.rationale: These names are shared owned models, enums, queries, and value objects whose Python-authored JSON representation must round-trip through Rust.
These constants and portable helpers require shared input/output or error vectors rather than owned JSON object fixtures.
Language signatures may differ, but these strategy-facing protocols and traits require matching behavior and consumer-boundary coverage.
These aliases name equivalent contract domains but have no independent runtime representation; owning surfaces provide evidence.
FallbackHandler is a Python Awaitable callable alias; Rust expresses the same call site with a generic Future closure rather than an exported alias.
NativeKernelUnavailable is an alias and NativeKernelUnavailableError is a language-native exception/error; parity is the failure category and message behavior at run_native_or_fallback.
These Rust support enums and aliases encode Python literal, union, object, or price-level domains and are covered through the owning fixture family.
ForecastRunLookup and OracleScoreDays are Rust representations of Python union-style method inputs and are proven through trait behavior.
Rust errors and FeeResult are language-specific carriers; parity compares normalized error categories at the helper boundary, not concrete exception identity.

Native consumer runtimes share this transport-ingress identity contract; its deterministic identity, revision, and collision behavior is covered by the Rust module tests and is not part of the strategy-facing Python API.

The allocation-sensitive borrowed kernel remains a separate contract whose actions, views, errors, and traits are proven by kernel contract tests rather than broad JSON fixtures. OrderStatusView predated SC-1 but was omitted by inventory drift; SC-1 classifies that unchanged borrowed view here and adds field-preservation contract evidence.
